title: 221(d)(4) Afforable Housing Training - HUD
description: The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) is issuing this source sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement for a contractor to provide training services to provide a structured, instructor-led, virtual training program tailored to FHA Section 221(d)(4) multifamily underwriting and affordable housing finance. The training shall strengthen participants' knowledge and practical application of FHA multifamily underwriting principles, including analysis of borrower and project financial information, market and appraisal data, property and capital needs information, environmental considerations, loan documentation, and multifamily lending risks. The Contractor shall be responsible for: Provide training materials that address the required learning areas identified in this SOW. Delivering live virtual instruction to HUD participants. Providing practical examples, exercises, case studies, scenarios, or other applied learning activities relevant to FHA multifamily mortgage transactions. Incorporating participant engagement methods such as discussion questions, knowledge checks, problem-solving activities, financial analysis exercises, or similar instructional techniques. Providing opportunities for participants to analyze and interpret information commonly used in FHA multifamily underwriting. Providing assessments or applied exercises to evaluate participant understanding of key course concepts. Providing documentation identifying participants who successfully complete the training requirements. Coordinating with the Government regarding the training schedule, instructional sequence, participant materials, virtual access, accessibility, and course administration. The Contractor may use commercially available training materials, customized materials, or a combination of both, provided the final training satisfies the requirements of this SOW and is not dependent on a proprietary certification or vendor-specific credential unless separately approved by the Government. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 611430, Professional and Management Development Training. There is no solicitation at this time. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to 1) provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; 2) secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements; and 3) implement a successful project management plan that includes: compliance with program schedules; cost containment; meeting and tracking performance; hiring and retention of personnel and risk mitigation. Based on the responses to this sources sought notice/market research, this requirement may be set-aside for small businesses or procured through full and open competition. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. Background: HUD staff involved in FHA multifamily underwriting, technical review, loan processing, and related program activities require a comprehensive understanding of large-scale multifamily lending and the information used to evaluate FHA-insured multifamily mortgage transactions. FHA multifamily transactions require consideration of borrower organizational structures, mortgage credit, financial statements, project income and expenses, physical property conditions, capital needs, environmental factors, market conditions, appraisal and valuation information, loan documentation, and lending risks. HUD staff must be able to analyze and interpret this information, identify material risks, understand how individual underwriting components relate to the overall transaction, and determine how the information affects FHA multifamily underwriting decisions. This training requirement is intended to provide HUD participants with structured and applied instructions that supports the development and enhancement of multifamily underwriting competencies. Training shall be aligned with applicable HUD guidance, including relevant provisions of the current MAP Guide, current approved HUD forms, and other applicable FHA multifamily program requirements. The training shall be aligned with applicable HUD guidance, including relevant provisions of the current Multifamily Accelerated Processing (MAP) Guide, current HUD policies and other applicable FHA multifamily program requirements (https://www.hud.gov/hudclips/letters/mortgagee) General Description of Work: Please see the Statement of Work (SOW) for specifics about the tasks associated with this effort. The Contractor shall provide a virtual instructor-led training program of approximately six to eight weeks in duration during the period of performance. The Government anticipates approximately two live virtual sessions per week, with each session lasting approximately two hours. Offerors may propose an alternative schedule, sequence, or delivery structure, provided the proposed approach satisfies the learning objectives and allows completion within the period of performance. The final training schedule shall be coordinated with and approved by the Government after award. Detailed descriptions of specific tasks are provided in Section 5.4, "Specific Requirements and Performance Standards� of the draft Government�s SOW � See Attachment 1. Interested vendors are those vendors who have interest in providing a response to RFI with ROM and who can provide a vendor capability statement demonstrating a commercial solution and technical experience for this requirement, including relevant scope in terms of its size, complexity and magnitude to the tasks/activities to be performed under this requirement, particularly, as it pertains to the support services and technical solutions required for the Federal Housing Administration Section 221(d)(4) multifamily mortgage insurance program for U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development staff. title: ATC Turf Field Maintenance
description: The objective of this contract is to provide comprehensive maintenance for fifteen (15) artificial turf fields located throughout Fort Jackson. The Contractor shall furnish all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and all other items and non-personal services necessary to perform turf field grooming, preventive maintenance, minor repair services, and unscheduled/emergency maintenance. Scheduled maintenance shall be performed bi-annually to ensure proper turf condition, safety, and performance. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Fort Jackson, South Carolina 29207 BASIS FOR AWARD: The Government will utilize a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) evaluation method for this requirement. The Government will award one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) C-Type contract to the offeror whose proposal is technically acceptable, has the lowest evaluated price, and is deemed responsible. The Government will evaluate the contractor's Technical Approach, Past Performance, and Price Proposal to ensure that it reflects a sound understanding of this requirement and complies with the requirements in the solicitation. A determination of a fair and reasonable price will be conducted. See attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-2 Evaluations. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Offerors shall submit a signed and dated proposal electronically in accordance with the attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-1 Instructions. Failure to provide all required documents or information may exclude the offeror from further consideration. Proposal Preparation Instructions. The solicitation instructions identify the following proposal volumes: a. Volume 1 � General b. Volume 2 � Technical Approach (to include Capabilities Statement) c. Volume 3 � Past Performance Information d. Volume 4 � Cost/Price EVALUATION: The proposal will be evaluated under three (3) evaluation factors: Factor 1: Technical Factor 2: Past Performance Factor 3: Cost/Price The Technical factor will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. An �Unacceptable� rating in any single Technical element will result in an overall rating of �Unacceptable� for Factor 1. Past Performance will be evaluated as described below. Price will be evaluated for reasonableness. See attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-2 Evaluations. Factor 1 � Technical: The Technical factor evaluation provides an assessment of the offeror's capability to satisfy the Government's minimum requirements. The Technical factor has three elements. The Government will evaluate the technical approach, quality controls, and key personnel qualifications related to providing preventive and unscheduled maintenance for fifteen (15) artificial turf fields located throughout Fort Jackson, SC. Element 1: Technical Approach and Understanding The proposal must demonstrate a clear understanding of and a sound approach to performing all services outlined in the PWS, including the specific basic services and tasks described in PWS Part 5. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must prove: 1. PWS Compliance: A compliant, clear operational methodology to perform multi-leveling field vacuuming, extensive fiber brush grooming, use of magnetic metal sweepers, and specialized synthetic turf cleaning/sanitization across the fifteen (15) synthetic fields. 2. Operational Responsiveness: A solid approach to executing scheduled semi-annual services and mobilizing personnel/equipment for unscheduled emergency repairs/maintenance in accordance with the response timelines set forth in the PWS. Element 2: Deliverables and Quality Control The proposal must address the deliverables listed in Technical Exhibit B and include the development of a Quality Control Plan (QCP) in accordance with PWS Paragraph 1.5.1. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must prove: 3. Reporting & Deliverables Compliance: A compliant administrative framework to compile, track, and electronically deliver all semi-annual reporting, worksheets, and documentation specified in PWS Technical Exhibit B. 4. QCP Framework: A draft Quality Control Plan (QCP) that completely addresses all requirements and criteria outlined in PWS Paragraph 1.5.1, such as lines of authority, deficiency prevention, inspection logging, key controls, and records preservation. Element 3: Key Personnel The proposal must confirm that all Key Personnel meet the minimum qualifications specified in the PWS. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must confirm: 5. PWS Qualifications & Experience: All proposed key personnel meet the minimum standards specified in PWS Paragraph 1.10. This includes confirming that the Contract Manager/Alternate has full authority to act on daily operations, and the Quality Control Manager and Systems Administrator each possess a minimum of five (5) years of direct experience. 6. Special Qualifications: Proof that proposed staff possess and maintain active Information Assurance Technician (IAT) Level I professional certifications as required by PWS Paragraph 1.10.d. Technical Factor Ratings: ACCEPTABLE � Technical Proposal meets the minimum requirements of the solicitation. UNACCEPTABLE � Technical Proposal does not meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation. Note: An "Unacceptable" rating in any single element will result in an overall rating of "Unacceptable" for Factor 1. Factor 2 � Past Performance: The past performance evaluation will assess the offeror's probability of meeting the solicitation's requirements as indicated by that offeror's record of past performance. Past Performance is assessed at the factor level after evaluating aspects of the offeror's recent (within the last 3 years) and relevant past performance, focusing on services similar to the Turf Field Maintenance requirements. The Government will evaluate past performance based on information submitted per the solicitation instructions and other available sources. Past Performance Evaluation Ratings: ACCEPTABLE � Based on the offeror's performance record, the Government has a reasonable expectation that the offeror will successfully perform the required effort, or the offeror's performance record is unknown. UNACCEPTABLE � Based on the offeror's performance record, the Government has no reasonable expectation that the offeror will be able to successfully perform the required effort. NEUTRAL � In the case of an offeror without a record of relevant past performance or for whom information on past performance is not available, the offeror may not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably on past performance. In the context of acceptability/unacceptability, a "Neutral" rating shall be considered "Acceptable." Factor 3 � Cost/Price: The Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total proposed price for all performance periods (Base Period plus Option Years 1 through 4). The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if the base period and option period prices are significantly unbalanced. As part of price evaluation, the Government will evaluate its option to extend services under RFO FAR Clause 52.217-8 by adding one-half (1/2) of the Offeror's final option year price (Option Year 4) to the Offeror's total evaluated price. Base Period Price (CLIN 0001) Option Year 1 Price (CLIN 1001) Option Year 2 Price (CLIN 2001) Option Year 3 Price (CLIN 3001) Option Year 4 Price (CLIN 4001) Evaluation of 52.217-8 Option Price (equivalent to 1/2 of Option Year 4 price) Offerors are not required to enter a separate price for the six-month extension period. Award will be made to the responsible offeror found to be technically acceptable with the lowest total evaluated price. title: 6630--LAB - VIRAL LOAD MOLECULAR TESTING CPT BRIDGE
description: Special Notice Page 5 of 5 Page 5 of 5 Page 1 of 2 This is a notice of the intent, not a request for quotes. Pursuant to the Revolutionary FAR overhaul (RFO), GSAM 538.7104-3 posting requirements, The Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA) on behalf of Veterans Integrated Services Network (VISN) 02 James J. Peters VA Medical Center, intends to award a sole source bridge award to Roche Diagnostics Corporation. Contractor: Roche Diagnostics Corporation Street Address: 9115 Hague Road City, State, Zip: Indianapolis, IN 46256-1025 The Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA), VISN 02, James J. Peters VA Medical Center requires a bridge contract to ensure the continuity of essential viral load molecular diagnostic testing equipment, supplies and services impacting patient care. The aforementioned contractor is currently performing under contract number 36C24226A0010 with the period of performance concluding on September 30, 2026. The anticipated period of performance for the bridge award is six (6) months, from October 1, 2026, through March 31, 2027, with one (1), six (6) month option period. The bridge award will be made under the authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) GSAM 538.7104-3(b)(ii); only one source is capable of providing the products and services required at the level of quality required because the products and services are highly specialized. As written, the DVAs requirement for molecular testing is able to be fulfilled through GSA s Federal Supply Class (FSC) Group 66 III. FSC Group 66 III, 605-6B was established for the procurement of clinical immunochemistry analyzers and corresponding tests and supplies; this group is a priority strategic source under Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO), and General Services Acquisition Regulations (GSAR) procedures, and as supplemented by the Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulations (VAAR). A long-term action was competitively awarded under FSC Group 66, from solicitation 36C24226Q0487 on a Cost Per Test (CPT) basis. Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) 36C24226A0041 was awarded to Roche Diagnostics on July 1, 2026. A bridge action is required to ensure continued CPT molecular testing, allowing Roche Diagnostics sufficient time to deliver, install, and validate the new analyzers under BPA 36C24226A0041, subsequently removing the current analyzers after validation (36C24226A0010). Market research obtained prior to the solicitation concluded that no subcontractors were/ are authorized distributors for Roche and/or capable of providing the level of supplies, equipment and services required for this action. Furthermore, no manufacturer exists with the ability to provide equipment, supplies and services for a period of six (6) months due to delivery, installation and validation time frames. Roche is the sole vendor capable of fulfilling a short-term action; a bridge award to Roche is a logical follow-on. This notice is not a request for quotes; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement which shall be considered by the Government. All capability statements must be received by no later than 12:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on September 14, 2026. Responses to be submitted to Lindsay Goldsmith, Contracting Officer at lindsay.goldsmith@va.gov. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

description: Le programme «CAJOU ± Compétitivité et durabilité de la filière anacarde en Côte d’Ivoire» vise à mobiliser des investissements publics et privés afin de renforcer la compétitivité, la durabilité et l’inclusivité de la filière. Il est cofinancé par: • prêt de la Banque européenne d’investissement (BEI) des Nations unies. • contribution de l’Union européenne au titre de l’IVCDCI — PAA 2026. • contribution de l’UNE de l’État ivoirien à travers le Conseil du Coton, Anacarde et Karité (CCAK). Le contractant sera chargé d’appuyer le CCAK et la Délégation de l’UE en Côte d’Ivoire, pour la mise en œuvre et le suivi des stratégies et plans d’actions nationaux dans le cadre du financement de la BEI. Les services en question seront mieux fournis par le prestataire de services pour les raisons suivantes (non exhaustives, éventuellement cumulatives): • Le haut niveau de spécialisation requis n’est pas disponible en interne; • Le besoin de flexibilité et la disponibilité nécessaire pour répondre aux besoins évolutifs et croissants. Le recours à des services de conseil externes est nécessaire pour répondre aux objectifs et aux besoins opérationnels de l’action et notamment i) afin d’accompagner le CCAK dans les défis en termes d’adaptation et de suivi du développement rapide de la filière; II) afin de suivre la mise en œuvre des stratégies et plans d’actions nationaux dans le cadre du financement de la BEI, iii) afin de renforcer les connaissances de l’ensemble des intervenants du secteur pour améliorer la pertinence, l’efficacité et l’inclusivité des politiques et stratégies de mise en œuvre.

description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR subpart 12.6, FAR 13 and supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. 1.0 REQUEST FOR QUOTE 1.1 The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-05. 1.2 Set aside is 100% Small Business. 1.4 NAICS: 541810 Advertising Agencies 1.4.1 Applicable size standard is $25,500,000 1.4.2 FSC: R701 Support � Management: Advertising 1.5 Period of performance: 21 September 2026 � 20 September 2027 1.6 Contract Line Item Structure (CLIN): College Insertion Orders for Advertising (lump sum) 1.7 Requirement details are in Attachment A - Performance Work Statement. 1.8 Applicable provisions and clauses are provided in Attachment B. 2.0 QUOTE FORMAT 2.1 Offers shall be submitted via email. 2.2 The offeror is expected to ensure compliance with all laws, regulations, standards, and any other constraints specifically identified in the solicitation. A statement of acknowledgement must be included in the quote to conform with all terms, conditions, provisions and clauses in the solicitation. 2.3 Company information shall include from sam.gov entity registration the 2.3.1 name and address (include �doing business as� (dba) name) 2.3.2 point of contact information (name, email and phone number) 2.3.3 UEI and CAGE codes 2.3.4 Tax identification number 2.4 The acceptable electronic format shall be compatible with Microsoft 365 or PDF Adobe. 2.5 All documents shall be labeled with the solicitation number (W912JB26QA003) and not be password protected. 2.6 The offeror should assume the Government has no prior knowledge of its capabilities and experience. The Government will base its evaluation on the information presented in the offeror�s quote. 3.0 VOLUME 1 - TECHNICAL CAPABILITY 3.1 The proposal shall present relevant information articulating the offeror�s proposed approach to meeting the PWS requirements. This section shall clearly demonstrate the offeror�s understanding by providing a clear description of the proposed approach to performing the work. The offeror�s description should include a clear description of all processes and procedures employed. Offers must submit a technical approach to include narrative of the quality assurance plan process. 3.2 Past performance of relevant experiences may be included as an example of how the technical approach has been previously performed. This information shall not be more than five years prior to the solicitation issuance date. Offerors shall provide relevant experience (for this purpose, experience refers to what an offeror has done, not how well it was accomplished) in performing proposed processes and procedures. 3.3 At least one of the recent past performance references shall include performance of the same or similar requirements as those described in PWS paragraph 5. 3.4 Provide a brief description of the work performed describing the similarities between the relevant work performed in comparison to the PWS paragraph 5. 3.5 The offeror shall not rephrase or restate the requirements but shall provide convincing rationale to address how the offeror intends to meet those requirements. 3.6 Technical capability and past performance will be used for evaluation. 4.0 VOLUME 2 - PRICING 4.1 Pricing shall be submitted in relation to the solicitation CLIN structure to include option periods if applicable. The total extended price shall be submitted for the period of performance. Quotes without the extended price may be rendered unacceptable. 4.1.1 The offeror shall include substantiating data of the price proposal to establish that the proposed price is reasonable and complete. The offer should include the burdened rate of labor and the applicable classification on the Department of Labor�s Wage Determinations. 4.1.2 Identify direct labor, other direct costs and an explanation of the escalation and how it was applied. 4.2 The offeror shall prominently list the expiration date of the pricing for a minimum of 60 days. 5.0 SAM REGISTRATION/JOINT VENTURE 5.1 The offeror must have an active registration on sam.gov at the time of award. 5.1.1 The registration must be active throughout the period of performance to be able to submit an invoice in WAWF. 5.2 In accordance with Class Deviation 2023-O0001 effective October 28, 2022, a small business joint venture offeror must submit, with its offer, the representation required in paragraph (c) of FAR solicitation provision 52.212-3, Offeror Representations and Certifications-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, and paragraph (c) of FAR solicitation provision 52.219-1, Small Business Program Representations, in accordance with 52.204-8(d) and 52.212-3(b) for the following categories: A) Small business; Technical capability will be established by evaluating the experience the contractor has with relevant and similar contracts. Technical approach and technical capability will be evaluated as acceptable or unacceptable. All factors are rated approximately equal. 7.3 The government intends to award to the responsible contractor whose quote, conforming to the solicitation, is most advantageous to the government based on price and other factors that provide the best value. 7.4 The government may award to other than the lowest priced quote if the factors of technical capability and technical approach provide the best value and exhibit betterments above the minimum requirements identified in the RFQ. 7.5 Negative or adverse information on FAPIIS or SPRS in the last three years may render your quote unacceptable. 8.0 AWARD 8.1 In accordance with FAR 12.207, a firm-fixed contract shall be issued. 8.2 Dates of period of performance will be 16 September 2026 � 15 September 2027 unless otherwise instructed. 8.3 The contractor shall communicate with the Contracting Officer Representative (COR) to schedule the preliminary performance. 8.4 A Pre-Performance Meeting on TEAMS will be held with the offeror�s point of contact, COR, contract administrator and contracting officer. title: Medicinal Chemistry Support Program for Therapeutic Development (MCSP)
description: This is a Small Business Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified business sources; (2) determine whether they are small businesses (e.g., 8(a), Veteran-owned small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owned small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, and women-owned small businesses); (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition; and (4) the availability of domestically manufactured and commercial services. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code should indicate its small business status in its response. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Small businesses are encouraged to respond. For equipment/supply requirements, responses must include the place of manufacturing (i.e. address if supply/equipment is a domestic end product and include country of manufacture). For equipment/supply requirements, small businesses must also address the size status of the manufacturer under the applicable NAICS code (i.e. address Non-Manufacturer Rule). Statement of Need and Purpose: The National Institute on Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) and the NIH Blueprint Neurotherapeutics Network (BPN) [https://www.nih.gov/neuroscience-blueprint], with participation from the Helping to End Addiction Long-term� Pain Therapeutics Development Program (HEAL-PTDP) [https://www.ninds.nih.gov/current-research/trans-agency-activities/ninds-role-heal-initiative/pain-therapeutics-development-program-ptdp], have established a �virtual pharma' network of contract service providers and consultants with extensive industry experience to enable therapeutic (e.g., small molecule, peptide, biologic) development in the NIH research community. This network offers researchers access to a range of industry-style therapeutic development services and expertise, including medicinal chemistry, IND-enabling studies, and Phase 1 clinical trial infrastructure, with the goal of supporting efforts to advance compounds successfully through Phase 1 clinical testing. The Medicinal Chemistry Support Program for Therapeutic Development (MCSP) component has the need to recompete its medicinal chemistry services to support a range of medicinal chemistry activities (exploratory, hit-to-lead and lead optimization phases) including project management and reporting, compound logistics, shipping, synthesis, computational chemistry/Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) and in vitro absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicology (ADMET) studies in support of preclinical drug discovery efforts supported by NIH, NINDS and its contributors. The ultimate goal of the NIH served by this program and of individual projects is to bring new drugs to market. To this end, the NIH has been granted a Determination of Exceptional Circumstances (DEC) to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) for this contract. The DEC enables the Contributors, Institutes that apply for a Grant, to retain control of the intellectual property for compounds created through the Medicinal Chemistry Support Program for Therapeutic Development (MCSP). Program Requirement: The scope of this MCSP program shall be medicinal chemistry services including project management and reporting, compound logistics, synthesis, computational chemistry and in vitro ADMET studies in support of preclinical drug discovery efforts supported by NIH, NINDS and its Contributors. NINDS requires a full service, turn-key medicinal chemistry operation for the development of therapeutics within the mission of NINDS, BPN, HEAL-PTDP and other NIH Institutes. The work may include any individual service or combinations of services including SAR analysis and design, synthesis, in vitro ADMET, computational chemistry/Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) and compound logistics of storage and shipping. Capable vendors must demonstrate the experience and capability to conduct from 1-10 projects simultaneously in the three chemistry stages: exploratory; hit-to-lead; and lead optimization. Capable vendors must also demonstrate the professional and technical personnel with appropriate experience and work history, appropriate facilities, resources and equipment, as well as the capability to rapidly scale up or down the number of staff dedicated to the MCSP contract, depending on the number of projects underway at any given time. Responses To This Notice Must Address/Provide The Following Information: Small businesses that meet the applicable size standard above and who believe that they possess the requisite capabilities, capacity, and personnel with the experience and qualifications to provide the full range of medicinal chemistry services described above are asked to address each of the areas described in the Program Requirement section below and to submit a response. Please ensure that your response is complete and sufficiently detailed to assist in our evaluation as to whether or not this requirement could be set-aside for small business participation only. (a) Current in-house capability and capacity to perform medicinal chemistry services (exploratory, hit-to-lead and lead optimization phases) including SAR analysis and design, synthesis, in vitro ADMET, computational chemistry/Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) and compound logistics of storage and shipping for 1-10 concurrent projects; (b) Demonstrated experience and success in providing a flexible medicinal chemistry support program optimizing compounds from hits into pre-clinical lead candidates by addressing a broad range of chemical liabilities, including toxicity, low blood-brain barrier penetrability, and metabolic instability by providing routine in vitro pharmacology and toxicology assays and services; (c) Demonstrated capability for productive collaborations with organizations and researchers involved in therapeutic development; (d) Staffing and personnel qualifications, i.e., numbers, availability and type of staff that could be assigned to such a program; their expertise, experience and education, including citation of any formal training; (e) A discussion of the requirements to be performed in-house versus those performed outside the responding organization; and (f) Your organization's name, address and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number; point of contact, including title, telephone number, and email address; and your current small business size status (e.g., small, small disadvantaged business, HUBZone, women-owned, 8(a), veteran-owned, etc. pursuant to the applicable NAICS code 541715. GENERIC MARKETING BROCHURES/CAPABILITY STATEMENTS WILL NOT BE EVALUATED. Please submit one (1) electronic copy of your response via e-mail to Shaun Rostad, at shaun.rostad@nih.gov and one Josh Lazarus, at josh.lazarus@nih.gov in MS Word (doc, docx) or Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF). The e-mail subject line must specify 75N98026R00144SB. You are encouraged to limit your response to fewer than 20 pages. ALL RESPONSES ARE DUE BY 1:00 PM EASTERN STANDARD TIME ON September 14, 2026. title: MIXED-METHODS RESEARCH PROJECT
description: The Public Diplomacy Section of U.S. Embassy Kingston intends to commission a multimodal public sentiment research effort to understand Jamaican adults� attitudes, motivations, knowledge gaps, and information-consumption patterns related to migration, including legal pathways and the risks and consequences associated with irregular migration. Findings will inform a data-driven, metric-oriented public diplomacy messaging strategy targeting priority demographic and geographic audiences in Jamaica. The research will support message development, audience segmentation, channel selection, and future performance measurement. The research shall be designed and implemented in a manner that protects respondent confidentiality, maintains sponsor anonymity during fieldwork where directed by DOS, and produces reliable evidence suitable for strategic communications planning. The successful Offeror shall plan, manage, and complete an integrated mixed-methods research project consisting of: (1) one nationally representative quantitative survey; and (2) one round of eight qualitative focus group discussions conducted across eastern and western Jamaica. The Offeror may perform the work directly or use disclosed and approved subcontractors. The prime Offeror shall remain fully responsible for all subcontractor performance, data protection, quality control, schedule compliance, and deliverables. The Offeror shall identify in its proposal all proposed subcontractors, the portion of work assigned to each, their qualifications, and the controls the prime Offeror will use to manage performance and protect information. Substitutions after award require prior written approval from the Contracting Officer. The primary objectives are to: Generate nationally representative quantitative evidence on migration-related attitudes, motivations, perceived benefits and risks, knowledge of legal pathways, exposure to misinformation, and trusted information sources; Generate qualitative evidence that explains the beliefs, emotions, experiences, social influences, and information environments underlying survey findings; Identify priority audience segments by demographic characteristics, geography, migration intention, media consumption, and other relevant attributes; Identify credible messengers, channels, themes, and message frames that may improve awareness of legal pathways and the risks of irregular migration; Provide actionable recommendations for public diplomacy messaging, content development, audience targeting, and future measurement; and Produce complete, well-documented datasets and methodological records that permit independent review and replication.

title: Airfield Electrical and Pavement Rehabilitation Upgrades_Moses Lake Auxiliary Field
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Seattle District (NWS), Special Projects Branch at Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), WA has issued this Sources Sought notice for market research purposes. The responses to this notice will be used to develop the Acquisition Strategy for an upcoming Request For Proposal (RFP) to perform airfield electrical and pavement rehabilitation upgrades at the Moses Lake Auxiliary Field. This is not a pre-solicitation announcement, nor an RFP. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this Sources Sought and no contract shall be awarded from this Sources Sought. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought or any follow up information requests. After review of the responses to this notice, and if the Government still plans to proceed with the acquisition, a separate synopsis may be published in the US Government System for Award Management (SAM) Contract Opportunities website at https://www.sam.gov. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to determine the availability, interest, and technical capability of qualified business concerns who demonstrated capabilities in meeting the project description listed below and to receive critical feedback from industry experts regarding the feasibility of the proposed schedule, staffing, and technical requirements. The proposed work is to be performed under the following North American Industry Classification (NAICS) code: 237310 � Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction. Both large and small business firms are encouraged to respond to this Sources Sought notice. However, if sufficient numbers of small business firms demonstrate interest, capabilities, and qualifications, the Government may choose to set-aside the acquisition for small businesses. For the purposes of this procurement, a firm is a small business if its annual average gross revenue, taken the last 3 fiscal years, does not exceed $45,000,000.00. For more information concerning NAICS and a SBA size standards, go to http://www.sba.gov. The following information is tentative and meant to provide interested firms with an idea of the general nature of the anticipated work. The Government reserves the right to update this information as project planning documentation is updated. The information below represents the most current information available and may be superseded upon publication of the preliminary planning information, which may be provided by the Government in the subsequent synopsis. Overview of Anticipated Contract: The Seattle District Corps of Engineers, under FAR Part 36 procurement procedures, anticipates issuing a Request For Proposal (RFP) and subsequent award for Construction Services to perform airfield electrical and pavement rehabilitation upgrades at the Moses Lake Auxiliary Field. The magnitude of construction for this project is estimated to be more than $10,000,000. Background & Scope of Work: The project involves the Maintenance and Rehabilitation (M&R) of airfield pavements and critical electrical systems on Runway 09/27 and Taxiway Foxtrot at the Moses Lake Auxiliary Field, located at Grant County International Airport (GCIA) in Moses Lake, WA. This airfield serves active U.S. Air Force tenant operations. Core Project Components: Pavement Rehabilitation: Demolition, grading, re-paving of Asphaltic Concrete (AC) and Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) pavements, crack repairs, joint sealing, and spall/patching repairs. Airfield Lighting Upgrades: Installation of new in-pavement light fixtures, augering light base locations, setting cans, pouring rapid-set concrete collars, laying new distribution paths, and pulling new #8 5kV conductors. Vault Equipment Upgrades: Complete overhaul of the remote military operations runway vault equipment, including rigging and mounting new Constant Current Regulators (CCRs), installing airfield lighting control and monitoring system (ALCMS) panels, and integrating Pilot Controlled Lighting (PCL) systems. SCHEDULE & CRITICAL PHASING CONSTRAINTS A key challenge of this procurement is the execution schedule. The Statement of Work (SOW) dictates strict operational constraints to minimize disruption to both military operations and GCIA�s active commercial runways: Airfield Closure Limit: The total airfield closure window is restricted to a maximum of 60 calendar days between April 1st and September 30th in a single construction season. Final cleanup and site turnover must be completed within this 60-day window. Phase 1 (West Taxiway F) Restriction: Must be completed within a 14-to-21-day maximum to minimize temporary closures of the adjacent active commercial Runway 04/22. Phase 2 (East Taxiway F) Restriction: Must be completed within a 14-to-21-day maximum to minimize temporary closures of the adjacent active commercial Runway 14L/32R. Standard Working Hours: Restricted to Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. However, 24/7 operations and overtime are authorized upon pre-approval and joint planning with GCIA and the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). Proposed 58-Day Electrical Milestones: The Government has developed a tentative 58-day electrical schedule within the 60-day closure window: Phase 1: Demo & Make-Safe (6 Days) � Isolate circuits, remove runway/taxiway fixtures, and demolish legacy vault equipment (ACE2, ALCMS). Phase 2: Trenching & Ductbanks (9 Days) � Trench RWY 9-27 distribution paths, lay conduit, and pour localized concrete encasements. Phase 3: Vault Equipment Install (10 Days, concurrent with Phase 2) � Rig/mount new CCRs, install ALCMS panels, prep terminal blocks. Phase 4: Pull Cans & Cabling (10 Days) � Set new pull cans with concrete collars; pull new #8 5kV conductors. Phase 5: In-Pavement Fixtures (8 Days) � Auger light base locations, set cans, and pour rapid-set concrete collars via on-site batch plant. Phase 6: Joint Sealing & Testing (5 Days) � Sawcut/seal concrete joints around light cans and perform Megger testing on all loops. Phase 7: System Commissioning (4 Days) � ALCMS integration, operational burn-in testing, and final turnover punch walks. STANDARD GOVERNMENT CREW ESTIMATES The Government's schedule assumes the deployment of three specialized, dedicated crews:. Crew A: Airfield Electrical (6 Personnel) � 1 Foreperson, 2 Journeymen, 2 Labors, 1 Equipment Operator. (Focus: Field demo, conduit laying, cable pulling, setting light bases). Crew B: Vault & Controls (3 Personnel) � 1 Lead Controls Electrician, 1 Labor, 1 Testing Tech. (Focus: Vault regulators, ALCMS, and systems commissioning). Crew C: Targeted Concrete/Civil (4 Personnel) � 1 Batch Plant Operator, 1 Equipment Operator, 2 Concrete Placers/Finishers. (Focus: On-site batch plant operations, ductbank encasements, pull can pads, light can grouting, joint sealing). A complete and final Statement Of Work (SOW) for the construction services required will be issued with the RFP. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Response to this Sources Sought shall be limited to no more than five (5) pages and shall as a minimum include the following information: � Name, addresses, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address and small business classification under NAICS Code 237310. � A brief capabilities narrative describing the interested firm's ability to meet anticipated contract requirements as described within this Sources Sought. title: Medicinal Chemistry Support Program for Therapeutic Development (MCSP)
description: This is a Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified business sources; (2) determine whether they are small businesses (e.g., 8(a), Veteran-owned small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owned small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, and women-owned small businesses); (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition; and (4) the availability of domestically manufactured and commercial services. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code should indicate its small business status in its response. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Small businesses are encouraged to respond. For equipment/supply requirements, responses must include the place of manufacturing (i.e. address if supply/equipment is a domestic end product and include country of manufacture). For equipment/supply requirements, small businesses must also address the size status of the manufacturer under the applicable NAICS code (i.e. address Non-Manufacturer Rule). Statement of Need and Purpose: The National Institute on Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) and the NIH Blueprint Neurotherapeutics Network (BPN) [https://www.nih.gov/neuroscience-blueprint], with participation from the Helping to End Addiction Long-term� Pain Therapeutics Development Program (HEAL-PTDP) [https://www.ninds.nih.gov/current-research/trans-agency-activities/ninds-role-heal-initiative/pain-therapeutics-development-program-ptdp], have established a �virtual pharma' network of contract service providers and consultants with extensive industry experience to enable therapeutic (e.g., small molecule, peptide, biologic) development in the NIH research community. This network offers researchers access to a range of industry-style therapeutic development services and expertise, including medicinal chemistry, IND-enabling studies, and Phase 1 clinical trial infrastructure, with the goal of supporting efforts to advance compounds successfully through Phase 1 clinical testing. The Medicinal Chemistry Support Program for Therapeutic Development (MCSP) component has the need to recompete its medicinal chemistry services to support a range of medicinal chemistry activities (exploratory, hit-to-lead and lead optimization phases) including project management and reporting, compound logistics, shipping, synthesis, computational chemistry/Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) and in vitro absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicology (ADMET) studies in support of preclinical drug discovery efforts supported by NIH, NINDS and its contributors. The ultimate goal of the NIH served by this program and of individual projects is to bring new drugs to market. To this end, the NIH has been granted a Determination of Exceptional Circumstances (DEC) to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) for this contract. The DEC enables the Contributors, Institutes that apply for a Grant, to retain control of the intellectual property for compounds created through the Medicinal Chemistry Support Program for Therapeutic Development (MCSP). Program Requirement: The scope of this MCSP program shall be medicinal chemistry services including project management and reporting, compound logistics, synthesis, computational chemistry and in vitro ADMET studies in support of preclinical drug discovery efforts supported by NIH, NINDS and its Contributors. NINDS requires a full service, turn-key medicinal chemistry operation for the development of therapeutics within the mission of NINDS, BPN, HEAL-PTDP and other NIH Institutes. The work may include any individual service or combinations of services including SAR analysis and design, synthesis, in vitro ADMET, computational chemistry/Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) and compound logistics of storage and shipping. Capable vendors must demonstrate the experience and capability to conduct from 1-10 projects simultaneously in the three chemistry stages: exploratory; hit-to-lead; and lead optimization. Capable vendors must also demonstrate the professional and technical personnel with appropriate experience and work history, appropriate facilities, resources and equipment, as well as the capability to rapidly scale up or down the number of staff dedicated to the MCSP contract, depending on the number of projects underway at any given time. Responses To This Notice Must Address/Provide The Following Information: Businesses who believe that they possess the requisite capabilities, capacity, and personnel with the experience and qualifications to provide the full range of medicinal chemistry services described above are asked to address each of the areas described in the Program Requirement section below and to submit a response. Please ensure that your response is complete and sufficiently detailed to assist in our evaluation as to whether or not this requirement could be set-aside for small business participation only. (a) Current in-house capability and capacity to perform medicinal chemistry services (exploratory, hit-to-lead and lead optimization phases) including SAR analysis and design, synthesis, in vitro ADMET, computational chemistry/Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) and compound logistics of storage and shipping for 1-10 concurrent projects; (b) Demonstrated experience and success in providing a flexible medicinal chemistry support program optimizing compounds from hits into pre-clinical lead candidates by addressing a broad range of chemical liabilities, including toxicity, low blood-brain barrier penetrability, and metabolic instability by providing routine in vitro pharmacology and toxicology assays and services; (c) Demonstrated capability for productive collaborations with organizations and researchers involved in therapeutic development; (d) Staffing and personnel qualifications, i.e., numbers, availability and type of staff that could be assigned to such a program; their expertise, experience and education, including citation of any formal training; (e) A discussion of the requirements to be performed in-house versus those performed outside the responding organization; and (f) Your organization's name, address and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number; point of contact, including title, telephone number, and email address; and your current small business size status (e.g., small, small disadvantaged business, HUBZone, women-owned, 8(a), veteran-owned, etc. pursuant to the applicable NAICS code 541715. GENERIC MARKETING BROCHURES/CAPABILITY STATEMENTS WILL NOT BE EVALUATED. Please submit one (1) electronic copy of your response via e-mail to Shaun Rostad, at shaun.rostad@nih.gov and one Josh Lazarus, at josh.lazarus@nih.gov in MS Word (doc, docx) or Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF). The e-mail subject line must specify 75N98026R00144SB. You are encouraged to limit your response to fewer than 20 pages. ALL RESPONSES ARE DUE BY 1:00 PM EASTERN STANDARD TIME ON September 14, 2026. title: Speed Trailers
description: The Government has a requirement for the procurement of two (2) 18-inch speed display radar trailers and two (2) 50-watt solar panels to keep them powered. Vendors are requested to provide a firm-fixed-price quote. The units must meet these salient characteristics: Radar and Display Characteristics: 18-Inch LED Digit Display: Ultra-bright, high-intensity amber (or multi-color red/yellow) LED characters that are highly visible from distances up to 1,000 feet. Radar System: Must be able to measure both approaching and departing directions (dual direction) with the ability to turn off or select one of those directions. 2. Power & Solar Configuration 50-Watt Solar Panel: Highly efficient monocrystalline solar panel mounted on a bracket to provide continuous trickle-charging to the battery bank. Battery Power Bank: Equipped with one (minimum) deep-cycle marine/AGM batteries (Group 24 or equivalent, around 80�100 Ah total capacity) to provide up to 7 to 14 days of autonomous operation without sunlight. Smart Charger: An onboard smart battery charger with an AC shore power outlet to recharge batteries manually when needed. 3. Construction & Physical Security Trailer Chassis: Built from rugged, heavy-duty welded steel tubing (typically 2-inch square 11-gauge steel) with a powder-coated, rust-resistant. Stabilization: Equipped with 3 or 4 retractable, adjustable jacks/stabilizers to lift the tires and secure the trailer in place, even in high winds. Vandalism Protection: Secure, lockable steel enclosure housing the batteries and controllers to prevent unauthorized access or tampering. Display Window: A durable, shatter-resistant, and UV-stabilized Lexan� or polycarbonate window protecting the LED face from road debris and vandalism. 4. Controller & Software Capabilities Local Controls: Push-button, rotary dial, or touchscreen local interfaces located in a locked enclosure. Automatic Brightness: Integrated ambient light sensor that automatically dims the LEDs at night to conserve battery power and brightens them during direct sunlight for visibility. Timers: Need auto shut off after an hour of usage in the event the unit is left on to prevent unnecessary battery drain, not necessarily a timing system with schedules.

title: USDA Forest Service Land Management Integrated Resources BPA (LMIR) Willamette NF, Detroit RD 2026 Reforestation
description: BPA Call Order Exceeding $20,000 Synopsis Requisition 117287 The USDA Forest Service (FS). Procurement & Property Services (PPS) is issuing this special notice as a means of complying with USDA Acquisition Regulation (AGAR), SUBPART 412.201-1, requiring that all calls above $20,000 be posted to the Government Point of Entry (GPE). The USDA FS intends on awarding a competitive BPA Call Order against the LMIR BPA to secure services for tree planting of Government-furnished tree seedlings in such a manner as to ensure tree survival and growth. 12363N23Q4023 The Land Management Integrated Resources BPA (LMIR) is a National BPA that consists of a large variety of work including Professional Services, Natural Resources Restoration, Project Management, NEPA, Communications, and more. The BPA can be utilized on all Forests and Grasslands and is available for all federal agencies to utilize. This is not a solicitation. This synopsis notification of intent to award a BPA Call order does not constitute a request for proposals or submission of any information in response to this notification. This procurement is restricted to those approved companies eligible for call orders under the Land Management Integrated Resources BPA (LMIR) for USFS. There are currently 140 businesses that will receive this solicitation. The Call Order shall be issued via email to those companies listed on the BPA. Any changes to the Call Order RFQ shall also be emailed to those companies listed on the BPA. Contracting Officer: William Ristoff william.g.ristoff@usda.gov This requirement will be competitively awarded as a BPA Call Order against the multiple award schedule BPA continuously solicited on the GPE at: SAM.gov. If contractors are not on the LMIR BPA and wish to join, they can respond to the BPA during the on boarding window which is Oct 1-Oct 31st each year for the life of the BPA. For instructions on how to join the BPA, search "Contract Opportunities" on sam.gov using solicitation number "12363N23Q4023" or emailing the LMIR BPA team for a list of on boarding instructions.

title: Powertrain Multiple Award IDIQ Recompete Solicitation Notice
description: The United States Air Force (USAF), 96th Test Wing (96 TW), Eglin AFB, FL is issuing a Solicitation for the recompete of the Powertrain MAC IDIQ. The purpose of this contract will be to provide the 96 RANSS/RNRT powertrain and component repair parts (both foreign and domestic parts) for its target assets to consistently maintain fully operational system that allow testing, characterization, analyzing, and evaluating weapons development and integration for the US Air Force. Powertrain and parts will be for foreign and domestic target assets. This requirement will be expected to utilize several different vendors to meet the need for powertrain overhaul, repair, and parts. The contract will be a multiple award IDIQ for 5 years with a 5-year Option for a possible total of 10 years. Each Delivery order will be evaluated using Lowest Price Technically Acceptable per line item. The contract will allow for on-ramping and off-ramping contractors in accordance with the Ordering Procedures. This Solicitation is issued in accordance with RFO 5.201, and RFO Subpart 5.2 and serves as the official Solicitation Notice for the Powertrain Multiple Award IDIQ requirement. Posted Solicitation date: 14 August 26. The intention is to competitively award this requirement as 100% Small Business Set-aside. The NAICS in question for this requirement will be 336992. Please ensure that your company is considered a Small Business under the requirements for that NAICS, otherwise you will not be considered eligible for award. The Intended PSC will be 2350. The Government will release the solicitation, including any subsequent amendments, on the SAM.gov website. No telephone or written requests for the Solicitation will be accepted. Amendment to the solicitation, if issued, will be posted to the same website. After solicitation release, vendors should regularly access the website to ensure they have all the amendments. Any questions about this Solicitation notice can be directed to Amanda S Lee, amanda.lee.13@us.af.mil, Satsuki Bowman, satsuki.bowman.2@us.af.mil, and Matthew Foil, Matthew.foil@us.af.mil. IMPORTANT INFORMATION: Offerors will be required to submit a Capability Statement. Registration in the Department of Defense DoD System for Award Management (SAM) database will be a prerequisite for receiving an award. As part of this solicitation for the MAC IDIQ the specifications for the first deliverable will be posted, as the first delivery order will be awarded immediately upon award of Multiple Award IDIQ contract to chosen vendors, please submit the proposal for the first deliverable as a separate submission. The Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) requirements do apply to this effort IAW RDFARS 252.204-7021 and 252.204-7025. The CMMC level required by this solicitation is: CMMC Level 1- Self-Assessment. This CMMC level, or higher (see 32 CFR part 170), is required prior to award for each contractor information system that will process, store, or transmit Federal contract information (FCI) during performance of the contract. The Contractor shall have and maintain for the duration of the contract a current CMMC Level 1- Self-Assessment or higher. Please complete a CMMC Level 1- Self-Assessment in Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) prior to award.

The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: USDA Forest Service Land Management Integrated Resources BPA (LMIR) Green Ridge PCT, Buck and Pile
description: BPA Call Order Exceeding $20,000 Synopsis Requisition 1169481 The USDA Forest Service (FS). Procurement & Property Services (PPS) is issuing this special notice as a means of complying with USDA Acquisition Regulation (AGAR), SUBPART 412.201-1, requiring that all calls above $20,000 be posted to the Government Point of Entry (GPE). The USDA FS intends on awarding a competitive BPA Call Order against the LMIR BPA to secure services for tree planting of Government-furnished tree seedlings in such a manner as to ensure tree survival and growth. 12363N23Q4023 The Land Management Integrated Resources BPA (LMIR) is a National BPA that consists of a large variety of work including Professional Services, Natural Resources Restoration, Project Management, NEPA, Communications, and more. The BPA can be utilized on all Forests and Grasslands and is available for all federal agencies to utilize. This is not a solicitation. This synopsis notification of intent to award a BPA Call order does not constitute a request for proposals or submission of any information in response to this notification. This procurement is restricted to those approved companies eligible for call orders under the Land Management Integrated Resources BPA (LMIR) for USFS. There are currently 140 businesses that will receive this solicitation. The Call Order shall be issued via email to those companies listed on the BPA. Any changes to the Call Order RFQ shall also be emailed to those companies listed on the BPA. Contracting Officer: William Ristoff william.g.ristoff@usda.gov This requirement will be competitively awarded as a BPA Call Order against the multiple award schedule BPA continuously solicited on the GPE at: SAM.gov. If contractors are not on the LMIR BPA and wish to join, they can respond to the BPA during the on boarding window which is Oct 1-Oct 31st each year for the life of the BPA. For instructions on how to join the BPA, search "Contract Opportunities" on sam.gov using solicitation number "12363N23Q4023" or emailing the LMIR BPA team for a list of on boarding instructions.

title: DFSP Bordentown, NJ
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice only. It seeks information from sources that can provide bulk and retail fuel services. No solicitation is being issued at this time. For reference purposes, this SAM notice is numbered SPE603-26-R-5X71. The amount of information available at this time is limited. This notice is also issued for the purpose of market research in accordance with Federal Acquisitions Regulation (FAR) Part 10. The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) - Energy - FESBA seeks potential qualified businesses that are able to provide services to discharge Government-owned aviation turbine fuel at DFSP Bordentown, NJ and transfer it to the Government-owned pipeline at the McGuire AFB, NJ. The DFSP Bordentown dock berth and mooring facilities shall be capable of receiving and berthing a barge not to exceed 4,200 deadweight tonnage (DWT), 300 feet length overall (LOA), with a minimum draft of 10 feet at mean low water from the dock to the open water. The facilities should be equipped with a turning dolphin capable of accommodating the lateral forces induced when turning a vessel and provide mooring points for barge mooring lines. The Contractor shall provide a detailed description of any port restriction/requirement, along with height restrictions from ships manifold to the waterline during loading, as well as a detailed schematic of the berth and mooring facilities showing the minimum and maximum capabilities to include current dredging charts for evaluation. The Contractor�s capability shall include all the necessary arrangements, permits, licenses, etc. to receive tankers and barges at the dock facility. This procurement will be unrestricted under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage) with a size standard of $36.5 million. The Government plans to award one firm-fixed price contract for a four-year based period, with three five-year option periods of performance and a possible extension not the exceed six (6)months. Responses are limited to not more than 5 pages. Any information provided to the Government as a result of this notice is voluntary. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. All responses to this notice are to be submitted by 3:00 p.m. local time Ft Belvoir, VA on September 14, 2026. Only responses submitted via E-Mail will be considered. E-Mail submissions to: Dominique.1.Vest@dla.mil. Interested companies should respond to the following: 1. A company profile to include number of employees, office location (s), DUNS/CAGE Code number, and a statement regarding current business status. Please note that registration in the SAM is required for DLA Energy contractors. 2. Capability of providing qualified and experienced personnel with appropriate clearances, if required. 3. Past Performance: Do you have past performance as a prime contractor or subcontractor on service contract for similar fuels management requirements? If so, please provide the following: Contract number, Name of Government Agency or Commercial Entity. Period of Performance, Dollar Value, Type of Contract (Fixed Price, Cost Reimbursement, etc.), and an explanation of services provided as they relate to GOCO fuels management. If your firm acted as subcontractor or joint venture, name the prime contractor or other party, the specific work performed and percentage. 4. Address any past performance problems, and resolutions taken. 5. Do you anticipate any type of teaming arrangement for this requirement? If yes, please address what kind of arrangement and what percentage of work, type (s) of service would you perform. 6. Does your company have experience with Service Contract Act of 1965 covered contracts? 7. Does your company have the financial capability and financial stability, and/or adequate lines of credit to sustain and support a five-year contract with multiple locations, in the event there are delays with the payment process? 8. What realistic phase-in period would you require to commence performance with personnel, equipment, and materials? This Source Sought Notice (SSN) is for planning and market research purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. The information gathered from this announcement will be used to determine if responsible sources exist and to assist in determining if this effort can be competitive. Furthermore, the Government will use the information, in part, to determine the best acquisition strategy for a potential procurement action and to assist in making future acquisition strategy decisions. This is not a request for quote or proposal. The Government does not intend to award on the basis of this SSN or reimburse any costs associated with the preparation of responses to this SSN.

title: Purchase and install of wall-attached telescopic bleacher system and removal of existing bleachers
description: Amendment to solictation FA813626Q0011: This solicitation is hereby amended to revise the product description from brand-name-only requirement to brand-name-or-equal requirement. 1. Products other than the specified brand name may be offered provided the proposed product meets or exceeds all stated salient physical. functional, and performance charachteristics outlined in the updated Statement of Work (SOW). Offerors proposing an equal product must identify the manufacturer of proposed product and shall provide suffient descriptive literature, specifications and other technical information neccessary for the Governmenrt to determine whether the proposed product meets the stated requirements. 2. The previously posted Statement of Need (SON) has been replaced by the Statement of Work (SOW). The SOW is amended to revise the Government's requirements from brand-name to brand-name or equal. The revision permits products manufactured by sources other than the originally specified manufacturer, provided the proposed product satisfies the Government's stated minimum requirements. 3. The previously applicable Brand Name Justification, supporting the brand-name-only requirement identified in the original solicitation is no longer applicable due to the revision of the governements requirement, and that document has therefore been removed from this solicitation. ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ The response deadline for this solicitation is 14 September 2026 at 2:00 PM CST. A site visit will be offered (optional) on 1 September 2026 so vendors can ensure accurate measurements. Questions are due 3 September 2026 at 2:00 PM CST. All interested parties should contact Lauren Rodgers, lauren.rodgers.5@us.af.mil and Contracting Officer MSgt Kristoforus Wenas, kristoforus.wenas.1@us.af.mil to schedule site visit. This RFQ is being issued on SAM.gov as a small business set aside. Purchase is required to satisfy Youth Center seating- � The current bleachers were installed 25 years ago and have reached the end of their service life. Replacement is necessary to ensure continued safety, reliability for all Youth Center spectators. The vendor will provide MAXAM telescopic bleachers manufactured by Hussey Seating Company, or equivelant, that will perform full installation of the system. The scope of work includes demolition and removal of the existing bleacher system. The new bleachers will be attached to the wall and designed to retract to extend maximum available floor space. System Classification � Brand & Model: Hussey Seating Company MAXAM Telescopic Series (or approved equivalent meeting identical dimensional and safety tolerances). � Design: Wall-attached, manually operated, multi-tier retractable spectator seating system designed specifically for indoor gymnasium environments. Physical Dimensions � Installed Length: Approximately 45 feet (45' total continuous length). � Fully Deployed Depth: Maximum 9 feet, 1 inch (9' 1") from the mounting wall. � Row Quantity & Spacing: 5 rows (tiers) of seating with a standard 22-inch to 24-inch row spacing to ensure adequate legroom and egress. Material & Construction � Understructure Frame: Heavy-duty, high-tensile structural steel shapes forming a rigid, self-supporting understructure, finished with a corrosion-resistant black powder coat. � Decks & Under-decking: Minimum 5/8-inch exterior-grade plywood panels with a durable, non-slip textured poly-wear surface overlay. � Seating Type: CourtSide collection (or equivelant) contoured HDPE (High-Density Polyethylene) seats, 10-inch (254 mm) depth, featuring an anatomical curved design with a front "waterfall" edge to alleviate thigh pressure. Demolition & Site Prep � Complete demolition and removal of existing 25-year-old bleachers with zero damage to surrounding walls, gym floor, or utility lines. � 100% damage-free. Any accidental damage must be repaired/restored to original condition at contractor expense within 5 business days. � 100% Inspection by COR and Youth Center Facility Manager. Operational Method � Operation: Manual operation utilizing a high-efficiency pull-handle/draw-bar system. � Tracking: Must feature self-supporting first-row wheels and structural guide tracks to allow smooth, single-operator extension and retraction without binding. � Operational Training: Provide comprehensive, on-site operational and safety training to at least five (5) designated Youth Center staff members. Accessibility Compliance (ADA) � Wheelchair Spaces: Minimum of four (4) integrated, ADA-compliant wheelchair seating locations recovered within the footprint. � Companion Seating: Adjacent companion seating structurally integrated as required by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and the International Building Code (IBC). Safety & Egress Features � Aisle Handrails: Center-aisle, self-storing, or removable structural steel handrails with round profiles, finished in high-visibility safety colors. � End Rails (Guardrails): Full-height steel guardrails at both open ends of the bleacher system, meeting a minimum lateral load requirement of 50 lbs/ft at the top rail. � Locking Mechanisms: Automatic mechanical tier locks that securely lock each row in the fully extended position to prevent accidental retraction during occupancy. Structural Load Standards � Compliance: Must conform to IBC (International Building Code) and ICC 300 (Standard for Bleachers, Folding and Telescopic Seating, and Grandstands) load ratings. � Active Live Load: Minimum 120 lbs/sq ft active horizontal framework capacity. � Sway Load: 24 lbs/linear ft parallel to seats; 10 lbs/linear ft perpendicular to seats. Execution & Safety Certification � Installation: Must be executed by a factory-certified installer. � Testing: Installer must conduct a formal structural and operational safety test prior to government acceptance. ***Additional requirements listed in attached SOW. Delivery/Services Required: The contractor shall be responsible for all freight and shipping costs to provide FOB Destination inside delivery to Tinker AFB, Oklahoma 73145. Delivery is required 60 days After Receipt of Order (ARO). Eligibility: The applicable NAICS Code for this requirement is 337127. The Product/Service Code (PSC) for this effort is 7195. This NAICS is the only applicable NAICS for this effort. To be considered for this award, contractor must have this NAICS on their profile. If it is not on contractor profile, request it to be added. In order to make a determination for a amall business set-aside, two or more qualified and capable small businesses must submit responses that demonstrate their qualifications and ability to perform in accordance with the Limitations on Subcontracting clause (FAR 52.219-14). Producuct Service Code: 7195 Pricing Arrangement: Firm Fixed Price

This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued.
